utterances.text: Since the objections of active combat were limited, I believed that they were objectively obtainable and that they would not pose a major problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you expecting to get such an order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never expected to get such an order before the day I actually got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let's move on one day, please. Can we have a look at P106. In fact, I'll stop that just now. Can we have a look at 7D1022 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, I am going to give you a hard copy of this because it's a very simple point I want to make, and it would probably be quicker for you just to read through it than for the document to be scrolled down through e-court. And I'll ask you the question in advance. This is the regular command report of the 1st of July, and would you just confirm that it makes no reference to any responsibility the brigade might have to put together a battalion for Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this regular combat report, there is no reference to Krivaja 95. At bullet point 2, refers to an order of the corps command dated 1st of July, 1995, and it says that the brigade should form a company that will become -- be put on the strength of the brigade that was supposed to be sent to the area of Glamoc which is the area of the 2nd Krajina Corps. Immediately on the eve of -- at the end of June, combat was taking place at this feature at the contact of Sekovici and Zvornik Brigade, and part of the Sekovici Brigade was also engaged in that area. So it was not feasible -- it was not probable that a new task would be given on the 1st of July, and it was indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can we -- before we go to the preparatory order, just have a look at the combat report for the following day, which is 7D0123. 1023. And I'll adopt the same -- oh, no, it's not necessary. It's a one-page document. You can read this on the screen. This is the regular combat report for the 2nd of July. Is there any mention of the brigade's responsibility in that report?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the bullet point talks about main tasks, but there are no tasks concerning Operation Krivaja 95.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we can see at the bottom of the document the time that it was received and processed. What time is that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't translated --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1715, that's when it was processed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we go to P106 please, the Drina Corps preparatory order for the 2nd of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, if we go to the bottom of it, I wonder if you could help us with the time it was dispatched and/or received and, if not, whether you can help us as to when during the course of 2nd of July, if it was that day, you first saw it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be blown up just a little? This document was sent on the 2nd of July at 1025.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, if we look under paragraph 2 and paragraph 2(a), it says that: "The 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade shall form forces equivalent to forces of a light battalion" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I am very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: "The 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade shall form forces equivalent to a light battalion with combat hardware and strong support for the conduct of activities along an independent axis." Had General Krstic told you that the number of men he was requiring you to contribute?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 2(a) makes a reference to the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. They were supposed to be equivalent to a light infantry battalion with the necessary combat hardwares and strong support. It is not a battalion as it should be by establishment. What it says here is that a temporary unit should be established tantamount to a battalion with all the necessary hardware and reinforcement. When you take all that into consideration, this would have been a tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how big is that in terms of manpower?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the strength of that unit was approximately 400 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Just before we go any further on the document, there is one point I forgot to deal with at the very top of the document. There are two dates there, the 2nd of July under the title "The Command of the Drina Corps," and the 3rd of July under the title "The Command of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade." Can you help us as to why those two dates are different, how that would have come about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we have seen similar documents so far with similar stamps or identical stamps. The document was drafted on the 2nd of July. It was dispatched to the Zvornik Brigade on the 2nd of July. It, indeed, arrived in the Zvornik Brigade on the 2nd of July. However, it was filed in the staff office of the Zvornik Brigade under a certain number and under the date 3rd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, can we go to paragraph 4 as there might be an important mistake we need to correct. The order was received by you in written form on the 2nd of July. How long did you have to put the forces together? In the English it suggests it's the 8th of July. Can you, firstly, have a look at the document in the original document and, secondly, tell us how long you actually had to get this force together so that we know.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original document reads the "2nd of July, 1995." Therefore, it's a mistake in the translation which reads the "8th of July" because it doesn't tell you all the other dates. When I received this preparatory order on the 2nd of July, I started drafting my own preparatory order and started forming the units that were to be dispatched to carry out the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So you had to get the battalion together or the light infantry battalion together the same day you received the written order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dead-line for the preparation of units for carrying out offensive actions was the 4th of July; therefore, I had the whole day on the 3rd of July to work in order to prepare these units and make them autonomous and ready to carry out the tasks along the designated axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Then you can help us, Mr. Pandurevic, what is the difference between forming units and conducting offensive activities?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Army of Republika Srpska had been established in the spirit of the professional standards, there would have been no differences. I would just issue a command for them to move because the unit would be in existence with all its equipment and means. However, what we were required here was to take from various units of the Zvornik Brigade, to single out elements from them, and to form a unit and prepare them. And only after that would we be able to send them to carry out the tasks that was required.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, we can all see it, but the preparatory order of the 2nd of July doesn't seem to tell you what you've got to do. Is that usual?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A preparatory order governs things in principal without providing any details. A unit is designated to carry out a task, a tentative area for the execution of the task, and the time as well is stipulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. Well, in straightforward terms, Mr. Pandurevic, what did you do on the 2nd of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 2nd of July, 1995, upon receipt of this preparatory order, I gathered my inner circle of the brigade command, and we jointly reviewed and studied the order, decided what our obligations were, and started drafting our own preparatory order which is also referenced here as well. In this order, I set down all the details that have to be resolved prior to sending the unit to carry out the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What do you actually do to form the unit?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're probably referring to some practical steps. I sent this order to my subordinate units, each battalion received their respective task in terms of how many men they have to make available. Elements of the Podrinje detachment who was in their base also had to assemble and prepare their equipment. That also referred to the logistics who had to do what their duty was. This was not done in one location. Some of the job was done in the battalion, some in the logistics department, and some in the Podrinje Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to the other thing you did concretely on that day which is P318, your preparatory order of the 2nd of July. This is a rather more detailed document about how your own unit was going to be set up. Who would you have sent this to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drafted this order pursuant to the order from the Drina Corps, and it is addressed to all subordinate units of the Zvornik Brigade whose duty was to make troops available for the execution of this task. In addition, it is also sent to the command organs my assistants because this order also implied certain obligations for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That is perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We left off -- and the document is still on the screen. The preliminary order drafted by you and dated the 2nd of July. Not much to ask you about that. The deputy commander is named as Milan Jolovic, he was rarely known as that name, he was more familiarly known as what?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a nickname, Legenda, and he came to the Zvornik Brigade with that nickname. That's not the one that I acquired there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if you could just tell us the structure of the unit you were -- the tactical group you were leading.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1 of this order shows that this tactical group had its command, one combat group made of the Podrinje -- or elements of the Podrinje detachment; combat group two, made up of two infantry companies from all battalions numbering about 60 men; an armoured and mechanized company; a battalion fire group; Howitzer regiment 122; and logistics element. All these elements made up a tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we go over to page 2, very quickly, we can see at 2.4, there was an armoured mechanized company which comprised a tank platoon, an armoured mechanized platoon, an anti-aircraft gun squad, and a handheld anti-rocket gun squad, and then a Howitzer platoon. How many men, in fact, did the tactical group comprise?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it had around 400 men, maybe fewer than that, but basically around that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thanks. Now, on the 3rd of July, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 3rd of July, following the formation of the command of the tactical group and the appointment of the commanders of combat groups, I organised my own commander's reconnaissance, and along with combat groups commanders and an operations officer from the command went and carried out the commander's reconnaissance in the area Pribicevac and Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to show you a couple of documents relating to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: First, 7D91.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I think we can deal with this fairly quickly, this page. What was the name of your driver during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Dragan Stevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what sort of vehicle were you being driven around in at that time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a jeep, Nissan Patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if we could just have a look, not for the last time, at the second page of this document which shows on the 1st of July Zvornik-Bratunac-Milici-Pribicevac, what does that journey record?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the day when we went to carry out commander's reconnaissance lead by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: On the 2nd of July, Zvornik local. But then on the 3rd of July, Zvornik-Bratunac-Zeleni Jadar, what does that journey record?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a journey to the commander's reconnaissance of the tactical group 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just a quick glance at 7D1098.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again under paragraph 2 we see: "Preparation of units for assignments in the area of Srebrenica, as ordered by Drina Corps command. "Relief of a unit in the Osmaci area. "Reconnaissance by commands in preparation for the next task in the Srebrenica area." Does that record what you were doing on the 3rd of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says that the command of the TGs going to -- or to make preparations for the next task in the Srebrenica sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We also see in that paragraph a reference to the Chief of Staff. And you told us that he had been injured during May and June. When did he come back to work?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was in Meljine on rehabilitation, which was the same institution where I was in 1994. I believe that he came back towards the end of June, but he was convalescing at home. I think that he reported back at the brigade on the 2nd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we move to the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we'll have a look at 7D242, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is a marching order. Who issued this?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What does a marching order actually mean?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A marching order, it's self-explanatory, it's an order which governs the way in which the unit to which this order refers to is going to march. Item 1 contains information about the enemy that might appear along the marching route. Then there is details relating to the unit carrying out the march, its strength, the starting point, the regulation points are determined, the end or the destination of the march, who is going to come out, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I think we all ought to just have a look at page 2 of the document so that we can see the route and ... The references to number 1 and number 2, what are they?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this order, the whole TG column was divided into two echelons; the 1st echelon and the 2nd echelon. Since the echelons were of different composition and were moving at different paces, then they had different starting times and arrival times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When did you leave the Zvornik Brigade barracks?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see exactly in this order when that was, but as far as I can remember I joined the 2nd echelon. The armoured mechanized company was the first, because it was the slowest, and I believe it was at around 1400 hours when I set off. You can see that the 1st echelon, as it's written here, will set off at 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what date was that so that we are clear?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pandurevic, you are going to turn around and start looking at a map in a minute. The rest of us will be able to see what you see on our screens, because we are going to upload a digital version of that map. And for everybody's information, they've all got their own disk of this map. It was disclosed as part of the supporting materials to our expert report and -- so everybody has their own disk, but we'll be able to follow it on the screen. Now, where did you march on the first day?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The march started on the first day on the axis Zvornik-Bratunac-Skelani-Jezero, and that involved the 1st and the 2nd echelons. The 3rd echelon marched along the Zvornik-Bratunac-Pribicevac routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did the 1st and 2nd echelon get to the by the end of the day on the 4th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 4th of July, in the early evening hours, the 1st and the 2nd echelons reached the village of Jezero, situated between Skelani and Srebrenica which is east of Srebrenica and Zeleni Jadar, a little bit closer to Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the 3rd echelon?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd echelon, after passing Bratunac, made a detour towards Pribicevac where they spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And on the following day?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following day, the 1st and the 2nd echelons, with whom I was, after we had spent the night in the village of Jezero, continued to March along the Jezero-Zeleni Jadar axis and deployed next to the Zeleni Jadar river.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, so that we can all follow this, you have the key to the map on the physical map there which we don't have because the map has been zoomed in so we can see the relevant area. Can you tell us, please, for those of us watching this on the screen, what the yellow arrows indicate?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The yellow arrows on the map behind me indicate the starting positions of the units that were planned to be used in Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the pink arrows?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pink arrows indicate their movement from the line and their advancement towards the Muslim positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The blue arrows?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue arrows indicate the positions and the axis of operations of the forces of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And lastly, the orange arrows?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orange arrows represent break through in-depth by forces taking part in Operation Krivaja 95 north-west of the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what activity were you involved in on the 5th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 5th of July, after the units arrived in the area of Zeleni Jadar, I personally went to the Pribicevac sector to see the 3rd echelon, which was the armoured mechanized company and the Howitzer regiment, and Major Milutinovic. I wanted to investigate the situation there and give them specific assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what other preparatory activity was taking place on the 5th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that on the 3rd, commanders of combat groups and part of the command were on the commander's reconnaissance, on the 5th group commanders reconnoitered their own axis of use.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What information or intelligence did you have as to Muslim positions in and around the enclave?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering that for almost two years these positions had not been moved and that on the opposite side were the positions of the Bratunac Brigade of the VRS and an independent battalion of Skelani, they knew very well where their positions were. They had a complete layout, and they have marked their firing points, and we were very well aware where the 28th Division troops were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what did you develop from that information, or what did your artillery units develop from that information?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In keeping with the information on the deployment of the 28th Division, I determined our own firing points for the 128-millimetre Howitzer platoon. This was in the area of Bukova Glava. From there one could observe the positions of the brigades of the 28th Division on my axis of attack. We drew up a sketch of the target. We determined all the elements, and when the attack started, we were ready to use our artillery to neutralise the enemy's firing points.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what other preparatory activity did the artillery unit engage in on the 5th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The artillery unit on the 5th of July reinforced its position. It cleared the wood and all the obstacles that were ahead of them for better reconnoitering, and they masked their own positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Explain that to us. What do you actually do to clear the wood ahead of you and make the firing easier?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to go in-depth, but I would like to tell you that there are certain conditions that a firing position has to meet. As far as the clearing of the wood goes, and as far as the clearing of the obstacles in front of the artillery tools, that meant felling of the trees, branches, so as to allow the gunner to find his aim.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When did the attack start?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early morning hours on the 6th of July, all the units of the tactical group were at their starting positions, and they launched the attack, all of them together. It was before dawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what activity -- what were the points of attack on the 6th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the axis of attack of the tactical group, there were two very important features. At the front part of the defence line of the 28th Division, and one feature was Biljeg and the other feature was called Tri Sise or three elevations without name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do we see those on the map that we have?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the map, this represents the command post of the tactical group, where it says BG1. This was the axis of attack against Biljeg, and this is BG group 2, or the direction of attack on the Tri Sise, so we were moving within the boundaries of this road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, as for this map, I understand that this does not have 65 ter number yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't believe it does. I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You refer to a disk, but I don't know how I can locate it among a lot of the disks. When was this map drawn?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It was drawn in preparation of our military expert report, so it was drawn last year sometime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could I ask by who?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Somebody, a military expert, commissioned to draw it. I mean, if you want a precise name, I will see what I can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You were pointing at two arrows. Are they the two arrows we see, as it were, moving either side of a yellow flag with a one on it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the arrows and one red one which then goes back towards the point from which it had originally started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What progress did you make on the 6th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of July, the forces of the 28th Division put up a strong resistance, and we did not manage to make any progress or push them back from their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was there any difficulty in conducting combat on the 7th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of July, in the evening after the failed attack, in the course of that day I wanted to regroup BG1 and 2 and continue on the 7th of July. However, the metrological conditions were very complex: There was a thick fog, rain, diminished visibility. So that on the 7th of July there were no combat activities. The forces were at a standstill on the positions that they had reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were the conditions any better on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of July the conditions were combat were much better, and combat activities thus continued. In the course of the 8th of July, we managed to take Biljeg feature and Tri Sise feature, and we created conditions for further advancement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In relation to Biljeg and Tri Sise, where were the 28th Division positions locations located?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions of the 28th Division were on the -- those two features. On the Biljeg feature there was also an UNPROFOR observation point. The positions of the 28th Division were in line with the UNPROFOR observation point. As for the Tri Sise feature, they were well reinforced.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did your tanks fire at the UNPROFOR observation post?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where did you stay on the night of the 6th, the 7th, and 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say that between the 4th and the 5th of July, I spent the night in a tent near Jezero, the next day in a tent near Zeleni Jadar, and the next two nights in a tent below Vukovar Glava. This was my command tent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When you took the positions at Biljeg and Tri Sise, what did the Muslim forces do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim forces withdrew in-depth towards the village of Ljubisavici, Zivko Brdo, and the Rajna feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did your forces encounter any UNPROFOR personnel at the point of taking those features?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did encounter the UNPROFOR observation post at Biljeg feature and in the Zeleni Jadar sector, at two points, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what happened on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was personally present at the Biljeg observation post. I encountered some soldiers of the DutchBat who were there. They were inside in the observation post. And pursuant to General Krstic's order, our instruction given to them was to go in the direction of Bratunac, and they said that we could take everything save for their combat vests. My order was that nothing should be taken from them and that the soldiers could be escorted via Pribicevac and sent away in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did any of your men take any property from UNPROFOR soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that observation post, which was well appointed, everything was in place for a comfortable life. My order was not to take any property. There were some bottles of mineral water, some food maybe. I don't know if any of my soldiers took any of those. I am not sure. But I did not allow my soldiers to take any of their combat gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What about the other point at which UNPROFOR forces were encountered?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Podrinje detachment forces were there, together with Legenda, they reported back that there were soldiers at that point, and the order was conveyed for them to go first to Pribicevac and from there to proceed towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now what happened on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th in the morning we continued combat operations. The TG forces managed to take Zivko Brdo feature as well as Rajna feature; and thus, they reached the planned line that we were supposed to take according to plan. Left from the forces of the tactical group, there was a tactical group from the 2nd Romanija, and the tactical group from the Bircani Brigade which later on took the planned featured Alibegovac and Kak, thus we managed to establish a line from which we could fully control the boundaries of the enclave and prevent any communication between Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I would just like to pause a moment so you can help us find those features on the map. Zivko Brdo?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the feature, and this is the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can't -- can't he point on the monitor or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, because it's not e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you help --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yeah. So could you help by describing where it is you're pointing to? We see what appears in English to be "TM" and a little blue -- what looks like a weather man's rain sign, right in the middle of the screen, and just to the left of that you see Zivko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we have problems, we will look at the video recording then. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We see -- do we see Rajna and Bojna on there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where the blue and pink arrows cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see a pointer here. Could you help -- if your case manager can help us. In the screen there is a pointer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Ah, the cursor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The cursor. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: There is Zivko Brdo. And if you move due north, you will see Rajna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And then above that, Bojna. Two more that we need to refer to, just trig point 780.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where is that, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it too well, I must admit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay. Well, trig point --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it should be on Zivko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And trig point 664, which is there.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just in front of or before Rajna feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, at that point -- we'll come to the order in a minute, but how did you regard the state of your task?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we look at the line which connects the trig point in front of Rajna feature, Zivko Brdo, and to the west, Vagan feature, then we get a new line with very strong and dominating features which completely blocks the passage of the 28th Division from Srebrenica towards Zepa. And in my view, this was the task that we were originally given pursuant to the instructions of Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. So can we now take the map away and have a look at P107.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And for Judge Kwon's benefit, he can find the map in two places. It's 7D100 -- 1066. It's also attachment 20 to Admiral Andric's expert report which is 7D891. And in this document I'd like to look at paragraph 5 in B/C/S, page 2, and English page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, under 5, these are the tasks to the units which were involved in this operation and also a task was given to the battalion from the 1st Zvornik Brigade, i.e., the tactical group. I don't want to go enumerating all the features, but the general axis was Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica along the asphalt road. And the task was to take Zivko Brdo feature, Rajna feature, and to reach the next feature in line, which was Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And while we're there, can you explain the phrase: "And be ready to continue the attack."

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a cliche which is used in all military documents such as combat orders, because an army always has to be prepared for ensuing combat activities of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, what did you do on the night of the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the night of the 9th of July, I organised a withdrawal of the Podrinje detachment from Zivko Brdo feature, and that feature was taken by the units of the independent battalion Skelani, and the units of BG2 from my tactical group remained in their positions during the night. I moved my tent to be closer to Rajna feature, and that's where I spent that night between the 9th and the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What happened the following morning, the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of July in the morning before dawn, there was a counter-attack launched by the forces of the 28th Division. They followed the general direction of Bojna-Rajna-Zeleni Jadar and the auxiliary direction Rajna-Pusmulici-Zivko Brdo. Those forces managed to push the forces of the tactical group, and they actually pushed us back almost to our starting positions, to the Tri Sise feature and the northern slopes of the Biljeg feature which means that we lost all the positions that we had taken the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where were you while that was going on?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in my tent when the counter-attack was launched. And then I went to the Zivko Brdo sector. I tried to consolidate the forces and stop the forces and stop the counter-attack; however, I failed. And I also withdrew to the Biljeg feature sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: About what time was it that you finished withdrawing, as it were?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tactical group was consolidated at the Tri Sise feature in front of Ljubisavici village on the northern slopes of the Biljeg feature above the asphalt road. And sometime around 10.00 when the Podrinje detachment had already been engaged, we were again ready to launch a new attack against the aforementioned features.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you speak to General Mladic on the morning of the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that conversation with General Mladic on the 10th. It was sometime before noon. We established communication via RUP-12.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where was he?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at the forward command post of the Drina Corps at Pribicevac feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what sort of mood was he in?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was taken by surprise to hear him on the radio. I did not have any previous knowledge about his whereabouts. I didn't know that he was there. I didn't know of any plans for him to be there. He was in a standard mood. His attitude was his familiar attitude. He did not want to listen to any explanations as to why the situation was what it was. His order was to urgently regain the lost positions and continue fighting, continue combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what did you say in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, I understand. That's what I said to him aloud, but I kept the real message to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What about the reversal you had suffered in combat, what did you say about that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I would do all I could and that we would regain the lost positions in the shortest possible time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We launched a counter-attack, we re-grouped our forces and launched an attack on Zivko Brdo and our auxiliary forces in the direction of Rajna feature along the road. And in the afternoon hours we managed to take Zivko Brdo feature again, and we proceeded towards Rajna and Bojna features.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to deal with a few stray pieces of evidence and see whether you can help us with them. On the trial video we saw, at one stage, your deputy commander, Milan Jolovic, shouting into a radio. When was that going on in the history of the fighting around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that video clip. Milan Jolovic was in Zivko Brdo area. He was commanding his troops, encouraging them, shouting, and trying to boost their morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But at what stage in the fighting, do you know?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat was underway. There was fighting very close to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you know what day it was?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was on the 10th during the counter-attack. Somewhere above Pusmulici village if my memory serves me right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, you've led me into my next question which is, how did Pusmulici village feature into the counter-attack on 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pusmulici village is situated directly beneath the Zivko Brdo feature, and that was one of the attack axes of the 28th Division, who, taking advantage of the poor visibility of the terrain, attacked Zivko Brdo. Therefore, later fighting broke out in Pusmulici, village and, as a result, one could see smoke coming from the houses in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of a Swedish settlement anywhere in the outskirts of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that building material for the construction of the Swedish settlement in the village of Slapovici was being transported in humanitarian convoys. It was to the west from the axis of my attack, and it was not in the line of my attack. From Zivko Brdo I was able to see this settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just one last small thing. I will ask you to look at this section of the trial video.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's P2047. And it begins at 1 minute and 8 seconds or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Open this bag, see what's inside. "And in this one? Well, I don't know. Here, have some. "There is some wine here."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's enough. We will stop that there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Whose car was that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my car. Or, rather, the vehicle belonging to the commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see in the video a signalman, my driver, my escort, that we stopped during the combat operations to have a snack or -- and a drink. You see that there is mud on the vehicle, and you can see a small section of the road. I can not be able to tell you exactly the position that we were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you know what day that was we see on the video?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, I haven't shaved, so it must have been a couple of days after the combat operations began.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So how did events finish on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, we managed to recapture the lost positions. We did that during the morning, and we also captured a new line on the Rajna feature, and we managed to get closer to the Bojna feature where the repeater was. I stopped there, and I spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, during the course of the 10th of July, had you received further orders -- or fresh orders as to what your objectives were?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received an order to proceed with combat operations and to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the latter part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, General Pandurevic, could you repeat the last part of your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received an order to proceed with the attack and to enter the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And who did you receive that order from and when?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure whether on the evening of the 10th, General Krstic was at the place where I spent the night and issued an order for us to continue in the morning towards Srebrenica. But I am quite sure that on the morning of the 11th, in the repeater sector of Bojna, all the units received details about the action that they are going take as part of Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just to clear up a small thing. When you talk about the repeater sector, you mean an area near a radio mask, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a tower. I don't know what was its purpose before and during the war. I think it was a relay for signal TV or any other transmissions. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've gotten a little ahead of me. Where did you spend the night on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the night on the 10th of July under the balcony of a demolished house by the road between the features Rajna and Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what happened on the morning of the 11th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the morning of the 11th, in the sector of the Bojna repeater, I was given specific tasks by General Krstic for further advancements towards the town of Srebrenica. And, for the first time, I noticed the soldiers from the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that task was given to you personally or at some sort of meeting?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a meeting. We were just stopping by the road, and General Krstic issued this order personally to me and orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was your understanding of the position within the town of Srebrenica itself by then?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was somewhat surprised by the further actions of the 28th Division in the wake of the counter-attack carried out by the VRS. The 28th Division forces did not try at all to reorganise their defence positions in front of the town itself; although, they had an excellent opportunity to do so in view of the layout of the terrain around the city or the town of Srebrenica. Had they done that, then it would have been very much difficult for the VRS to enter the town. My task was to continue operations along the road, to reach the town, and to capture the surrounding hills, the hills surrounding the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What did you understand was going on in the town by the morning of the 11th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part of the town that we were able to observe from our positions was completely empty. We didn't see anyone in the town. We were able to hear radio communications of the 28th Division. And our impression was that they were retreating in panic towards northern parts of the town and that, in effect, they were also leaving the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did your radio reconnaissance reveal them talking about anything else?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By listening in into their communications, we revealed that they were on the retreat and also that they had information or instruction to put as much distance between them and us because the NATO bombing campaign was ensuing. One could feel that they were gloating because of this impending situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we just have a look then, please, at the trial video again, P2047 [Realtime transcript read in error "P0247"]. This time at 4.05 to 4.25.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Not even the NATO backed -- could harm unprovoked plans of the Western European alliance engaged against the Serb forces of Srebrenica. Destructive plain bombs, however, did not demoroalise our soldiers. On the contrary, they lifted the moral of the members of the Serb army. On the other hand" --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. That will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The -- were there bombs dropped from the sky that day?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This video shows one aerial bomb being dropped on the south edge of the town because the very entrance into the town is very steep, and the bomb landed next to the jeep of Captain Legenda. What you cannot see in this footage, there was an ambulance which was also damaged by the bomb. I and a group of officers were on the right-hand side of the road, some 60 metres from the vehicle that had been hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think we will leave it there, if that's all right with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to suggest that to you because I see that you are moving into -- onto ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just to correct a number, the trial video is P2047.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. We will reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
